utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, please, appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin and Daryl Mundis, assisted again today by our intern Jaspreet Saini, and Mr. Andres Vatter, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll ask the Defence for appearances now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Defence for Mr. Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, and my legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Defence of Mr. Kubura, Mr. Rodney Dixon and Nermin --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't catch the name, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish good morning to everyone; Prosecution, the Defence, and Mr. Dixon, who is hidden behind the monitor. Good morning to both the accused and all the personnel of the courtroom. We are to continue today with cross-examination of the witness. Will the usher please bring him in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General. The hearing is continuing today with continued cross-examination. I'm therefore giving the floor to Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, over the course of last evening, I reviewed my notes, and I do have a few additional questions with respect to the time you were in the courtyard on the 11th or 12th of June 1993. And of course, by "courtyard," I mean the courtyard of the monastery in Guca Gora. The persons that you saw there that day, do you recall what type of clothing they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have spoken already about this. They had varied clothing. Some wore jackets, camouflage-uniform jackets. Some had mismatched trousers. Some wore traditional clothing. They were not uniformly dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, I would ask that the witness be shown an excerpt of one of the videotapes, which is P482. Before we do that, however, I would like to explain to the general a little bit about this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, we have a videotape which is in evidence, and I'm going to show you a clip that runs about a minute and a half to two minutes. This videotape shows some persons inside the church at the Guca Gora monastery. I'm fully aware that you said on that day you were not inside the church. I'm showing you the tape to ask you if you recognise any of the persons inside the church as being among the persons that you saw on the 11th or 12th of June 1993 in the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems there is no sound. No sound?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, you mean on the videotape? We will not play any of the sound. We will simply show the videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, I understand you were not inside the church, and when we get to the clip, it does show the interior of the church. What I will be asking you about is the persons inside the church, if you recognise any of those persons as being the person or persons that you saw in the courtyard on that day. Do you understand what I'm asking you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I completely understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask, General, that you, with the assistance of the usher, if we can put it so you can see the videotape on the screen in front of you. And perhaps if you do see any person that you recognise, if you could just tell us, and we will attempt to stop the videotape at that point in time. It may not be possible to do that. We may have to show you the videoclip more than once. But if you do see anyone that you recognise from that day, I would ask you to please just tell us at that point and we will do our best to stop the video at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, Mr. President, this is an excerpt from P482.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General Merdan, did you recognise any of the people that were shown in that videoclip?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not recognise in this videoclip anybody from the group that I talked to. I talked mainly with the interpreter out of that group. Only one among the group communicated. The rest were standing around without communicating. Only one of them spoke through the interpreter, and I cannot recognise him in this picture, or rather videoclip that you have just shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, you told us on, I believe it was Thursday of last week, that you recall a certain meeting held at the 3rd Corps headquarters where General Halilovic was present, and the issue of foreigners was discussed.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, you have in the packets that we handed out yesterday, Prosecution Exhibit P794, which is photocopies of certain pages of the 3rd Corps war diary. I also have the actual physical, original war diary, which might be easier for the witness to look at than the photocopies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, could you turn, please, to the tab that's marked P794.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, if it would be of assistance, we do have the original for the witness to look at if it's clearer than the photocopy. With the assistance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You'd better give him the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask the usher, perhaps, to show that to the Defence, and then provide it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm presenting you with a notebook. And first, let me ask you if that notebook looks familiar to you.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen this book in this form. Or rather, format before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems there is a transcript problem. We don't see a transcript on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Nor do we, Mr. President. I believe the technicians are...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the text. We have the text on the screen of the computer, the laptop, but not on the monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you just told us that you have not seen this book in this format before. Can you perhaps elaborate on that.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have this book in my hands for the first time, and I'm seeing it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you that this is the 3rd Corps -- one of the 3rd Corps war diaries, or war logs, and you're telling us you've never seen this document before, or this book before?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: True. I never have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us on Thursday -- or Friday of last week that you had reviewed on occasion the logbooks maintained by the 3rd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have reviewed only part of the records of the 3rd Corps. The records of the 3rd Corps are humungous. Many days would be needed to review the entire documentation on the 3rd Corps. I reviewed only a part of it. I also testified before this Court that I had no time to review all the reports, daily, combat and other reports, let alone the entire documentation of the 3rd Corps. You have to understand that the documentation of the 3rd Corps is enormous. It was the work product of special organs, and all I know is that they kept special records for operational organs, security organs, and other organs of the 3rd Corps. Each had separate records. I could not see all that they combined have written. And about this war log before me, I can only say that I haven't seen it. At least, I think I have not seen it until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you told us about different units or departments that kept such logs. Can you tell us, based on perhaps the cover or title page of this book, what department this log belonged to or was compiled by?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know in principle that a war log is kept by a department within the staff of the 3rd Corps, the section for operations and training. I can see who has signed below.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. Can you tell us who signed this book.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, "Concluding with the 14th of May 1993," 97 pages. But I cannot recognise the signature. I can only say that it is not mine. I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. don't know who signed this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you to turn to page 70 of this diary. Actually, if you could, sir, at the top, I would ask you to look at the page with the stamped number 01814064, which I believe is the page opposite the handwritten page numbered 70. Are you looking at that page, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, General, approximately what time did the meeting that was attended by General Halilovic begin?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember at what time that began. I testified that it was held late at night. I don't remember when it began or when it ended, but it was held late at night. It began late at night. I cannot remember the exact time. I said I couldn't even remember the precise date. If I remember correctly, it was on the 20th or the 21st. I gave that as a rough date, and I also gave a rough time frame, but I could not remember the exact time of the beginning and the end of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, if you would look now at the preceding page, that is, the page with the number 69 at the top, the handwritten page, do you see at the top it indicates 21 April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the date, 21st of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could then turn the page to, again, the page with the stamped number ending 4064, I would ask you, sir, to look down about two-thirds of the way down that page, you see an entry that begins 2330. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see on the left at the bottom, it says 2330.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And below that and continuing on to the following page, there is a list of individuals and their functions that were present on the 21st of April 1993 at 2330 hours. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from this log you could conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask you, sir, if you could just read through the pages that depict or that are put forth in this document that concern this meeting on the 21st of April 1993 commencing at 2330 hours. If you could just briefly read through what's contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have finished reading the text that you instructed me to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, to the best of your recollection, do the minutes as reflected in these written pages convey what occurred at the meeting late on the evening of 21 April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the meeting is reflected in these minutes as far as I remember the topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could go back to the page again with the last four digits 4064, and this is the page where the meeting minutes began, where you saw the numbers 2330. Are you on that page, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you look down the list of participants to where you see the name Sakib Mahmuljin. Do you see, sir, that he's listed as the secretary to the commander of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I ask you this question, sir, because you told us on the 9th of December that you do not believe Sakib Mahmuljin was a member of the 3rd Corps in July 1993. That was at page 68, line 16, of the transcripts on the 9th of December. This 3rd Corps diary that you have before you seems to indicate that Mr. Mahmuljin was, in fact, a member of the 3rd Corps as of 21 April 1993. Can you perhaps explain that to us, if, in fact, he was on that date?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I can say that at that time, Mr. Mahmuljin was not a member of the 3rd Corps. I can interpret this in the following way: This is a wrong wording, because in the 3rd Corps, there was never a secretary. According to the establishment, the duty of a secretary did not exist and it did not exist in practice. I can view this from another angle maybe. Sakib Mahmuljin was introduced to us as a member of the office of the Supreme Command. Maybe the person who authored the diary on this day - I don't know who it was, I can't recognise the signature - maybe he didn't understand too well when Mr. Mahmuljin was being introduced. I remember that he was introduced as a member of the office of the commander of the Supreme Command Staff rather than a member of the 3rd Corps. And I can claim with full responsibility before this Trial Chamber that Sakib Mahmuljin at that time was not a member of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, we had another witness who testified before this Trial Chamber who told us that in June 1993, he saw Mr. Mahmuljin's name listed in a 3rd Corps telephone directory, with the functional title of "advisor to the 3rd Corps commander." Can you comment on that aspect.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that anybody introduced Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin as an advisor to the commander of the 3rd Corps in my presence. If somebody had indeed presented Mr. Mahmuljin as the advisor to the commander of the 3rd Corps, then you have to ask that person. In my presence, this was never done. I told you how Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin was presented in my presence, how he was introduced to me. I can repeat that just to confirm what I remember. In my presence, Sakib Mahmuljin was introduced as a member of the office of the commander of the Supreme Command Staff, and this is what I knew at that time about Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin. Whether Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin had a dual position, I wouldn't know. You have to ask people who knew. I can only tell you what I know and what I can remember, so I can only claim with full responsibility that Sakib Mahmuljin at that time was not a member of the 3rd Corps. He was in the 3rd Corps; however, he was not the advisor to the commander of the 3rd Corps, as far as I can remember. Actually, I cannot remember anybody having been in that position. Nobody was the advisor to the 3rd Corps commander. I didn't have that information; in practice it wasn't the case. It is not customary in the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to have an advisor to the commander. I really don't have any information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, at lines 11 and 12 of the current page of the transcript it, said, "He was in the 3rd Corps." Now, can you tell us what position Mr. Mahmuljin had in the 3rd Corps and the time period he had that position.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already testified about that. I remember this period of time when I was told what the position of Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin was. As far as I can remember, the first position he held in the 3rd Corps was the position of the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps. Before Mr. Mahmuljin, the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps was Mr. Muradif Mekic. I can't say exactly when was it that Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin was appointed the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps, but I believe that this was in the early autumn. I can't remember the exact date, but I'm sure it wasn't in April 1993. In the month of April of 1993, he was not a member of the 3rd Corps, and he did not hold a position in the 3rd Corps. I would like to underline once again, as far as I know, Mr. Sakib Mahmuljin was appointed the chief of staff of the 3rd Corps. Before that, he did not hold any positions in the 3rd Corps, and he was not a member of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to clarify, sir, you say you believe he was appointed the chief of staff for the 3rd Corps in the early autumn. Would that be the early autumn of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was referring to the autumn of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, General, during the time period of June 1993, was there, in fact, some kind of 3rd Corps telephone directory or listing that had the personnel of the 3rd Corps with phone numbers on how to reach them?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there was a telephone directory listing the most important staff of the 3rd Corps. I also believe that on that list there were some other people who could be contacted via the 3rd Corps, which doesn't mean that they were members of the 3rd Corps. I can talk about that. It is possible that there was such a list of names; in other words, a directory, in the 3rd Corps. It was a long time ago. I can't remember exactly, but I accept this possibility that this might have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall ever seeing Mr. Mahmuljin's name listed in that telephone directory with the functional title of "advisor to the 3rd Corps commander"? Did you ever see that in the 3rd Corps directory?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember this detail. When I wanted to get hold of a number of telephone to call somebody, I had a service below my level, the service that operated telephones. I never gave them the number when I needed to talk to somebody; I gave them the name of the person that I wanted to talk to, and this was the service that called that person. I can't remember having had in my hands such a telephone directory in which the name of Mr. Mahmuljin would be listed. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let me turn now to a different topic. Again, however, it concerns the monastery in Guca Gora. You told us last week that you returned to the monastery with Father Radic, the Catholic priest. Do you recall the approximate time period when you visited the monastery on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I visited the monastery in Guca Gora with a delegation, a mixed delegation, headed by the European Monitors. And I also already said that as far as I could remember, Mr. Landry Remi was the head of the delegation, and I also said that Father Radic was a member of that delegation. I've also testified that, as far as I can remember, this was at the beginning of August 1993. We set off from Zenica. I don't know what the time was. I assume that we arrived in Guca Gora around noon or an hour earlier or maybe an hour later than that, but I believe that it was around that time. I can't remember exactly. I can't even remember the date. However, I remember the delegation very well. I remember the names of the people, but I cannot give you the exact date, and especially, I can't give you the precise time when we visited the monastery in Guca Gora. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, General, on this occasion, at the beginning of August 1993 when you visited the monastery, did you observe any military police or any military checkpoints controlled by units of the 3rd Corps in the immediate vicinity of the Guca Gora monastery?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the military police. However, I didn't know whether it was the military police of the 3rd Corps or of the 306th Brigade. In any case, I saw members of the military police who were standing around the monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you see any other soldiers of any units of the 3rd Corps in addition to the military police that you saw on that day?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I understand your question. When you say "member of the 3rd Corps," are you referring to some other units of the 3rd Corps? Are you referring to members of the army in general? If you mean troops of a unit of the 3rd Corps, I did see soldiers. I don't know how many, I didn't pay too much attention to that. I focussed my attention on the delegation that I was a member of. Our goal was to comply with the requests of the European Monitors and Father Radic to visit the church. I didn't pay too much attention as to who was moving around us. I've told you that, as far as I remember, I saw the military police. There may have been other soldiers, I'm not excluding that possibility, but however, I did not pay too much attention to that. It was 11 years ago. It is possible that there may have been men in uniform who were members of one of the units of the 3rd Corps. I'm not ruling that possibility out. However, I can't remember. I can't restore the picture of how things were at the time around the monastery, whether there were any other soldiers or not. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, on that occasion, at the beginning of August 1993, did you go into the church?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did go into the church at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you also on that occasion go into the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether we entered the church from the south or from the east, through the courtyard and then on to the church. I can't remember how we entered the church. I only know that we did enter the church. I believe, however, that we entered through the main gate, which is on the south side of the church. I can't be a hundred per cent sure of that because I can't remember. I believe that it was on the south, that we used the south entrance to the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, can you please describe for us with as much detail as you recall the condition of the interior of the Guca Gora monastery church in early August 1993 when you visited.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that we entered a somewhat larger room. I believe that that room was the room entered by Catholics to -- who wanted to pray together. The interior of that room was damaged. I've already said that on one of the walls, I saw fresh paint. It looked as if somebody had painted this wall in a haste. What was underneath that paint, I couldn't see, I couldn't read. However, I did notice that something was painted over. The fresh paint did not match the background. So one could easily see that something had been painted over. I did not observe any other rooms in any great detail. I kept standing in that big hall. I didn't walk around to inspect everything. I could just see what I could see from that place where I was standing. I did not visit all of the rooms in the monastery to inspect what the condition of other rooms was. I can only tell you what I can remember and what I saw when I entered this main, big hall, which is quite a large hall. I could not see precisely what the condition of the monastery was. I only saw that this part was damaged, but the damage was not major.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please elaborate what you mean by "the damage." You've told us that apparently something was painted on the hall and then covered up with fresh paint. Other than painting on the hall, can you recall any specific damage to the interior of the Guca Gora monastery's church?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that there was an inscription on the wall. I only said that the wall had been painted over and that the fresh paint did not match the background. This is what I could observe. This is what everybody else could observe. Because it was the biggest difference to the rest of the room. There may have been some dirty spots on other parts of the walls, I can't remember. This is what I meant when I said minor damage. I thought that this was easily repairable. The fresh paint that was applied on the wall in a haste could have been repaired rather quickly and could be matched with the rest of the wall without any problems. That's what I meant when I said there was minor damage. Whether there was any other damage, I don't know. I didn't pay any attention to that. My only goal was to make the delegation feel safe, to allow the delegation to see everything. I did not personally strive to see everything and to inspect the extent of the possible damage in the monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, do you also recall seeing any damage to the courtyard or the walls of the courtyard or the contents of the courtyard, including any sculptures? Do you recall seeing any damage to any of those items or places?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you notice any damage to the exterior of the church building itself?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really sorry for not being able to remember. If I had paid attention and if I had noticed any damage, I would tell you. I'm not excluding that possibility. However, I've told you that I did not pay any attention to that. I've told you what my mission was. My mission was not to inspect damage and to assess the level of damage in the church. If that was -- if that had been my mission, I would have taken a piece of paper and a pen, and I would have noted it down. I believe that I was carrying out my mission properly by escorting the mixed delegation and by taking care that they felt safe. That was my main mission on the day. It was not my mission to record the level of damage in the monastery and in the church. If my mission had been that, I'm sure I would have recorded everything because that's the kind of person I am. If I am given a mission, then I record everything, and then I provide arguments to my observations. I believe that my mission was not that at that moment. I've told you what my mission was. I was not trying to observe the details that you are mentioning at the moment. I just saw the damage that I've described to you, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I understand your mission was to make sure the delegation remained safe, but the fact of the matter is you were at an extremely important cultural and religious site in Central Bosnia, the Guca Gora monastery, and you went there with a very prominent member of the Catholic clergy from Central Bosnia to show these people the condition of the Guca Gora monastery. Isn't that why you took Father Radic to the monastery, to show him that in fact it wasn't damaged?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I understood my mission was to allow Father Radic to see what he wanted to see. And I believe that I carried out my mission on the day. I allow the possibility of the outer walls of the monastery having been damaged. You have to bear in mind that there had been fighting in the vicinity of the monastery and that the monastery was very close to one of the -- to the main road leading through Guca Gora. And I know that in the month of June, there was fighting in that area. It is possible that the outer walls of the monastery were damaged. I respect and value religious buildings a lot, and wherever my mission carried me, I tried to prevent people from damaging religious buildings irrespective of their religion. And I believe that I carried my mission out in accordance with the instructions and with my orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, we're going to move now to a different subject altogether. And this concerns the small town or village of Mehurici. I asked you yesterday about your presence in Mehurici in February 1992 in the context of the Patriotic League meeting. Do you remember we talked about that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did talk about it, but I don't remember that we said it was in February 1993. It was in February 1992. If I said that it was in February 1993, then I misspoke and I apologise to this Trial Chamber. This meeting took place in February 1992 rather than in February 1993. It was a year earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not want words to be put in my mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, my question was February 1992, and there's no one putting words into your mouth about 1993. I simply asked you if you remembered yesterday we spoke about you being in Mehurici in February 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 1992, in the general area of Mehurici. When you speak to common people, then they refer to this area as Mehurici. However, the meeting did not take place in Mehurici itself. It took place in a different place. To be more precise, in a different location within the general area that people refer to as Mehurici. It is the local name for a broader area that people up there call Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: What building or hamlet or physical place on the ground did you have this meeting in February 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can be very precise on that. I can show you the house where the meeting was held. We were moving towards the village of Mehurici, and very close to the centre of Mehurici there is a bridge as you enter the village. Before that bridge, we turned right along the banks of a little brook. We arrived in Zagradje, and then we turned right along a road which is rather steep. We arrived at a lonely house, and it is in this house that the meeting was held in February 1992. I remember that very well because I went back to the vicinity of that house after the war. There is now a memorial plaque on the house to mark the date of that meeting which was held in February 1992. So I know very well where this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. took place, and I can show you very precisely where that house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps after the break, we will endeavour to get a map and I might ask you to mark this house. But for now, can you tell us which direction this house was from the centre of Mehurici. Was it south of Mehurici, north of Mehurici? Southeast, northwest? East? West? From the centre of Mehurici, where was this house?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can visualise it at this moment, this entire situation, from the centre of Mehurici, it was to the northeast. But I would more easily orient myself with a map, a large-scale map, so that I can define the locality more precisely. I think it's to the northeast of Mehurici, the centre of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, let me ask you, other than this point in time in February 1992, were you in Mehurici at any other point during 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember passing through the area close to Mehurici on my way to Visnjevo village. I cannot remember which date it was exactly, but it was certainly in the first half of 1992. Whether I visited some other time in 1992, I can't remember. It didn't seem important enough for me to remember any other passage through that area or visit to Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall being in Mehurici in the first six months of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember precisely within that specific time frame. It's a long one, after all, six months, and I already testified before this Court that I passed by Mehurici village at least two or three times. At one point I said that I passed very close to Mehurici when I was going to Miletici village in April, on the 25th of April 1993. I also testified before this Court that I passed by driving in an UNPROFOR vehicle through the Biljana valley as part of a joint commission from Vitez, the joint commission that we discussed at length. I also testified that I passed through Biljana Valley also in my capacity as the member of joint command, when we were talking about Travnik. I also said that I don't know how far I went in Biljana Valley on the 8th of June 1993 to attend the meeting of local communes. I believe I testified about this passage through Biljana Valley. And it was very close to Mehurici, so one of these times could have been in the first half of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, I appreciate that answer, but my question wasn't whether you passed by Mehurici on a number of questions; my question was were you actually in the centre of the village of Mehurici at any point in time in the first six months of 1993? In the village of Mehurici itself. Not in the region, not passing by, but in the village of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't rule out the possibility that I was there. But if I may add, it must have been an important event for me to go to Mehurici. But I can't remember any important event that would have required me to go to Mehurici. I don't rule out the possibility of having been there, but I cannot claim with any certainty that I was there on such and such day, on such and such an assignment, on such and such a mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you again so that we're 100 per cent clear, the last -- I'm talking now about the last six months of 1992, from, say, 1 July 1992 through 31 December 1992. During that six-month period, were you in the village of Mehurici? And again, not the area, not the region, not passing by, but in the village of Mehurici from 1 July 1992 to 31 December 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? From June to December 1992? Or did you say 1993? I'm not quite clear on this, which year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: 1992. The second half, the last six months of 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember going there in the last six months of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, during the last two months of 1992 and into 1993, where was the headquarters of the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1992 and in early 1993, when the 306th Brigade was established, the command post of the brigade was located in the building of the mine. That place is called Han Bila, if I remember correctly. I know very well where the building of the mining company was, where the headquarters of the brigade were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, was there a command post or a battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade at the school, the primary school, in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried very hard to know exactly where my command posts of brigades and of operation groups were. I tried to memorise details even on a lower tactical level because, after all, the battalion command is on a lower level, and I don't rule out the possibility that the headquarters of one of the battalions was in the primary school. But I had never visited that particular headquarters in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall where you were on the 31st of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean, the New Year's Eve?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that just before the new year, I inspected the battalion near Turbe. I remember that very well. It was the hardest front line, the defence line of the town of Turbe, because it was an access to the town of Travnik. I remember that well because it was the hardest line, near the petrol station in Turbe. I remember I was there on the New Year's Eve in the night of the 31st December 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you inspected or visited the 306th Mountain Brigade on the evening of 31 December 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't rule out the possibility, but I remember that forward defence line because in the entire area of responsibility, right after the 3rd Corps was established, it was the hardest defence line. And it is quite understandable and logical that I should have inspected that forward defence line because it was so difficult. And even if I had gone there, I didn't think of it as important. My mission was to visit the troops. I spent a long time at the forward defence lines speaking to the troops, trying to speak to every soldier. You can imagine at a moment like that, what a high-ranking officer could talk about with the troops whose life was constantly on the line because the shooting never stopped. I thought it was the right thing to do, and that's why it stuck in my memory, that date, I mean. I don't rule out the possibility that I dropped by that place, but it was hardly as important as inspecting the forward defence line. That was really the most difficult and the most important in the area of responsibility that I was the commander of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, I ask you this question because the war diary of the 306th Mountain Brigade contains an entry on 31 December 1992 at 1935 hours that indicates that you visited the command of the 306th Brigade on that evening at that time.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said I didn't rule out the possibility. For that brigade, it must have been a memorable event if I had been there indeed, that they would have written it down in their war diary, their war log. I don't rule out the possibility. If it's written in the war log, then it's probably true. But I told you what my main mission was. I always focus on my principal mission, the principal mission given me. And I don't rule out the possibility that I might have also visited the command of the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And had you visited the command of the 306th Mountain Brigade, where would you have gone? Where would that have been on 31 December 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had been my mission to visit that brigade command, then I would have certainly prepared myself for that mission just as I had prepared myself to visit the forward defence line. I was wearing a Kevlar vest, knowing the kind of mission I was going on. And if I had been given the mission to visit the brigade command, I would have certainly -- I would have certainly known that and written that down in my notes. You could look through them, if you like [as interpreted]. I know what my main mission was, and I was quite happy with my mission for that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you've just mentioned your notes. Did you, in fact, keep a personal diary or a notebook during the time period 1992 through 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I kept my personal notes, not in the form of a diary or anything. Those are really very intimate, very personal notes, including some very personal things, and they don't necessarily reflect the chronology of events. Those are very, very personal notes that I kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, you just told me at line 3 that we could look through them if we like. And I'm wondering if you have these notes with you perhaps in your bag that you bring to Court with you every day.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot allow you to view my private, personal things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know how it was interpreted. I'm just seeing this for the first time now, but the witness did not say at any point that he could allow anybody to review these notes. I'm just going to check the transcript. It says, "You could look through them, if you like." That's something that the witness did not say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Line 3, page 24, it says in English: "You could look through them, if you like." But it seems he didn't actually say that. So General, did you say in your language - because maybe it's just a misinterpretation - that your notes could be reviewed? Or is it the case what you said at the end, that it's out of the question to review your notes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are my very personal notes, and showing them to anyone is out of the question. These notes are something that I view from time to time, and I don't allow even my family to read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's go back, then, sir, to the issue of the 306th Mountain Brigade. I want to be very clear on this: At any point in time from Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. November 1992 through June 1993, were you ever in the primary school in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that within that period I went to the primary school in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you ever notified or informed by anyone that there were foreigners on the upper floors of the primary school in Mehurici in 1992 or early 1993? And by "foreigners," again, I mean armed foreigners.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no such information ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that several hundred metres away from the primary school in Mehurici, the foreigners established a camp in the Savici settlement or the Poljanice area, several hundred metres south of the Mehurici primary school? Did you ever become aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never learnt about that. I have already said that I did not know where those foreigners were located. And we defined yesterday what we understand by this term "foreigners." So I did not know they were located in those houses in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, last week you told us that on the 8th of June -- and I'd like to talk to you a little bit about the 8th of June 1993. On the 8th of June, you told us that you were in the Bila Valley, but that you left at some point in the early afternoon to return for an important meeting in Zenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said I couldn't remember the precise time, but sometime around noon I received information that the Ovnak pass had been liberated on the axis where units from the 3rd Corps were involved in joint action. So I went there to check and I spent very little time there. I remember crossing that Ovnak pass and going down into the Bila River Valley, and then went straight back because I had very important commitments in Zenica and had to return to Zenica by early afternoon. Whether it was 1.00 or 2.00 p.m., I can't remember, but in any case, I had to return to Zenica. I can't remember now whether I actually reached -- how far I actually went. I can't be precise. But I noticed that it was time for me to be heading back. I don't know up to which village I actually went, but I had to go back rather soon. I remember that much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, let me see if I can help refresh your recollection, because I suggest to you that on the 8th of June 1993, you certainly got as far as the village of Mehurici and that you were in Mehurici on the 8th of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I couldn't rule out any possibility. I don't know how far I went that day. On that day, I didn't communicate with anyone. Maybe you have information that somebody saw me. That's possible. But I remember very well that I didn't speak to anyone. I had no time to linger long enough to speak to anybody. I don't rule out the possibility that I was seen by anybody. If you have such information, of course I will not deny that it's possible. I'm certain that I didn't go to the school or near the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, do you know an individual by the name of Munir Karic who was the assistant commander for logistics in the 306th Mountain Brigade? Do you know Mr. Karic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Mr. Karic. For a while he was commander of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember meeting with him on the premises of the forestry department cafe on the 8th of June 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where that cafe is. I can't remember that detail. I only remember that I didn't speak to anybody. I don't rule out the possibility. But I certainly didn't go into any catering establishment, any tavern, any cafe. I had no reason to go to such places. I don't drink alcohol. And it's hardly possible that anybody saw me inside a cafe. I didn't go to any cafes that day. I don't even know where that cafe is that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, I'm going to read you a passage from the transcript and ask you your reaction to that when I'm finished. This commences at page 11.505 of the transcripts, from 10 November 2004. This is Mr. Karic testifying. Question: "Do you know the reason why you met Mr. Merdan when he was arriving in the afternoon? Did you personally meet him?" Answer: "Very briefly." Question: "Did you talk?" Answer: "Well, we did talk. But I asked him what direction he had come from, and he said he had come from -- I don't remember now. Some direction. He had a sandwich to eat, and that was it." My question -- that's the end of the transcript, and it runs to the first line of page 11.506. My question, sir, is: Is it your testimony that Mr. Karic was mistaken about seeing you? Because he does go on to line 7 of page 11.506, and say, "I met him" - meaning you, sir - "on the premises of the forestry department's cafe." Is Mr. Karic mistaken about what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that anybody is wrong, especially not Mr. Karic. I can't say he got it wrong. But I can remember only what I can remember. I remember that I came from the direction of Zenica, and I can't remember saying this to him at all. At that moment, it must have been much less important to me than to Mr. Munir Karic. It could not have been in the afternoon, anyway. It could only have been before because I had to return quickly to Zenica. And I told you already all I remember. I don't rule out the possibility that I was seen by somebody, and now you quoted back at me Mr. Karic who did see me. A lot of people saw me. I can't deny that. I just told you where I was and when I was there. I can't remember the conversation with Karic in particular, and I can't remember that canteen of the forestry department. I told you that, as a rule, I very rarely go to cafes and such places. Whether I had something to eat on that occasion, I don't know. I don't remember whether I did or not. And Mr. Munir Karic knows that I occupied a high position, and in his eyes it must have been an important thing to meet with me. To me it meant nothing. I don't remember at this moment whether I saw Mr. Munir Karic and whether I talked to him. And if he's saying that I did, then I can't say that he's lying. I'm just saying that I don't remember. That doesn't mean that I'm saying that he's not telling the truth. In those cases when I remember something clearly and I remember the date, I say so definitely, but I don't remember this meeting with Mr. Karic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do note it's time for the break. Sir, I will have one or two extra questions for you after the break about this, and then we're going to move on to the kidnapping of the HVO officers, including Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We shall resume at 11.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. During the break, the Prosecution was able to print out a map, and I would ask -- I've shown this to the Defence during the break. I'd ask that this map be shown to the witness and perhaps put onto the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, before the break, you were telling us you could perhaps locate the house where the February 1992 meeting concerning the Patriotic League was held. If you're able to see the location, I would ask you to point to it using the pointer.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have looked at the map. I can tell you that the school in Zagradje is here, and this is the road leading to the school, right to this road. I don't know whether this road here on the map - I don't know when this map was drawn - but it would be somewhere around here. If this is the road, then it would be somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be provided with a thin blue marker. He could perhaps circle that location and perhaps put the letters "PL" for Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]. [Interpretation] This would be the approximate location. So if I could mark that with a circle, this would be the approximate location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. Do you recall -- was this in someone's house, this meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a private house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who was the owner of that house, or who lived in that house?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when this meeting was held, there was nobody in that house. The owner lived there just for a short period of time, but he left. The meeting was held in the absence of the owner of this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall the name of the owner of the house?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could please put today's date, 14 December 2004, on the bottom or the top of that map and sign your name on the map.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let me turn now to the period in mid-April 1993 when the HVO officers were kidnapped. You've talked about this, and Zivko Totic was kidnapped. Do you remember testifying about that last week?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember testifying about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, you told us about the steps that you took following the kidnapping of Zivko Totic, and I'd like to ask you some follow-up questions concerning that kidnapping. Now, you told us on the 9th of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. December that the indications that you had were that the perpetrators were foreigners and that no one from the 3rd Corps was involved. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that at the moment when the kidnapping took place, we did not have any information as to who had perpetrated that act. After a certain time, we were informed by the European monitors that it was probably foreigners who had committed the act because the foreigners were in communication with the European monitors, and they asked for an exchange of the foreigners who had been arrested and who were kept in the HVO prisons. That's what I testified to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall the date that the first of the HVO officers were kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the date was the 13th. I remember that on the 14th of April 1993, we went to look for the kidnapped soldiers of the Novi Travnik HVO Brigade. I believe it was on the 14th, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, sir, you believe that the kidnapping was on the 13th of April 1993, and on the following day, the 14th of April 1993, you went with a group of other persons searching for these kidnapped HVO officers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were kidnapped on the 13th. I know that on the 14th, if I'm not mistaken, a mixed commission went out to search for the HVO officers from Novi Travnik. And that I know because at the meeting of the joint commission, it was said that the HVO officers had been kidnapped, and I said immediately, "No problem. Let's see where they are." We inspected a large area. It was a commission consisting of the European monitors, Mr. Franjo Nakic was there on behalf of the HVO, and I was there on behalf of the army. And that's the way I testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, just so that we're all clear, the HVO officers from Novi Travnik, that did not include Zivko Totic? He was kidnapped a few days after the HVO officers from Novi Travnik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know who the kidnapped persons were. It was Mr. Franjo Nakic who told me that at our meeting. And what Mr. Franjo Nakic told me on that day did not include Mr. Zivko Totic as one of the kidnapped persons. As far as I remember, Mr. Zivko Totic was kidnapped later, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's talk about the 14th of April. You told us that you went with Mr. Nakic, and I believe you also told us that there was at least one international person, whether from the European monitors or BritBat. Was it the European monitors who went with you, at least one of them, on the 14th of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 14th of April, there was a representative of the European monitors there. I believe that his name was Valentino. I believe that he was from Spain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Excuse me. Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that his name was Juan Valentino.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the 14th of April 1993 when you and Mr. Nakic and Mr. Valentino went searching, where exactly did you go?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to those places where the representatives of the HVO, that is, Mr. Nakic, thought that they might have been taken to. On that day, we went all the way up to Ravno Rostovo because they thought that they might have been taken there. We went all the way to Ravno Rostovo to see whether that was correct. Mr. Nakic, the European monitors, and myself inspected those premises and did not find any kidnapped members of the HVO there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were informed that the -- by the European monitors that they believed that foreigners were involved in this kidnapping.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that moment, I didn't have that information. At that moment, four -- the foreigners did not take responsibility for the kidnapping of the HVO officers from the Travnik Brigade. No, the European monitors didn't say that on that day. It was Mr. Franjo Nakic who said that there were indications and information that they had been kidnapped and taken in the direction of Ravno Rostovo. Even Mr. Franjo Nakic didn't say anything as to who had kidnapped the HVO officers. At that moment, nobody mentioned who the perpetrators of the kidnapping might have been. They only said that they were kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, where did the information or indications come from that foreigners were involved in the kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information reached us quite a number of days after that date. It was then that the 3rd Corps was informed that they had been in contact with the foreigners who had committed a kidnapping and who wanted to exchange these people for their friends who had been arrested and kept prisoner by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Why, sir, did you go to Ravno Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to Ravno Rostovo because Mr. Franjo Nakic told us that there were indications that the kidnapped soldiers had been taken either in the direction of Ravno Rostovo or to Ravno Rostovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, just a moment ago when I asked you about the information or indications that foreigners were involved, you said, "This information reached us quite a number of days after that date. It was then that the 3rd Corps was informed that they had been in contact with the foreigners." When you said "they had been in contact with the foreigners," who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the European monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the 14th of April 1993, when you went to Ravno Rostovo, what unit or units of the 3rd Corps were in Ravno Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of April 1993, a company of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the 1st Battalion was in Ravno Rostovo. And that's at least what we were told by the local commander, who was billeted in that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, I suggest to you that on that date, it was the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, and at that time, that unit was commanded by Ramo Durmis. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware who the commander of the 1st Company was. But the man who said that he was the local commander of that unit at that moment at that facility did not introduce him testify as Ramo Durmis. I don't know this person, Ramo Durmis. I'm sure that he did not introduce himself as Ramo Durmis. If he had mentioned his name or his position, I would remember that very well. I'm sure that he only said he was the commander of that company, but he did not mention his name being Ramo Durmis, and that is the truth. And I'm sure that Mr. Franjo Nakic and the European monitors heard that. This man certainly did not introduce himself as Ramo Durmis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So to your recollection, he simply indicated that he was the commander of the 1st Company and left it at that? Is that what you recall?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. Don't put words into my mouth. I said that there was a company there. I didn't know that it was the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion. He said that he was the local commander of the company of the 1st Battalion. He didn't say that he was the commander or that that was the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion. This is not what I said. Please don't put words into my mouth because this is not what I said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, where did you go in Ravno Rostovo, looking for these kidnapped HVO officers from Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand, how we went there. You mean what means we used to go there? I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, sir. Once you were in Ravno Rostovo, did you simply drive around the village to see if the HVO officers were wandering in the streets, or did you go in any buildings or did you look anywhere in the village? Where did you go in Ravno Rostovo looking for these HVO officers from Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no village where we went. It's just one facility. Before the war, it used to be a motel. We entered that building. We did not see any HVO soldiers there. This is not a village, this is just a facility which used to be a motel before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, where did you speak to this local commander, this local company commander that you've told us about? Where did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spoke to this local commander in that facility, in that building, in the motel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how long did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for long. I can't be sure of the time, but it was a very short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than Ravno Rostovo, did you go on that day to other locations? And if so, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, after Ravno Rostovo, we returned to Novi Travnik, to the brigade command which was in the new hotel in Novi Travnik. After that, we were taken to the premises of the military police of the HVO of Novi Travnik, and this is where we were kept until late in the night. On that day, we did not inspect any other areas in order to search for the kidnapped officers of the HVO brigade from Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the time that you went to Ravno Rostovo, did Mr. Nakic or Mr. Valentino say to you that they believed that the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was involved in these kidnappings?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Neither Mr. Nakic nor Juan Valentino ever told me that members of the 7th Muslim Brigade took part in the kidnapping. They didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you recall any of the specific discussions or questions that were asked of this local company commander in Ravno Rostovo by yourself or Mr. Nakic or Mr. Valentino?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the presence of Mr. Franjo Nakic and Mr. Valentino, I spoke to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the local commander who introduced himself as the local commander. And I explained what our mission was. He told us that he didn't know that members of the HVO had been kidnapped. I remember this well. We asked him to inspect the premises. He said that there was no problem, but he also said that he did not have any information about HVO members having been kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did anyone ask him about the presence of foreigners in Ravno Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember anybody raising that issue. As far as I can visualise this scene at this moment, I'm not sure, and I don't believe that anybody raised this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you now, sir, to focus your attention on the Totic kidnapping and not these four or five or however many HVO soldiers or officers from Novi Travnik. My next questions will focus on the kidnapping of Zivko Totic. Where were you, sir, when you first heard that Colonel Totic had been kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of April 1993, I was on my way back from a meeting in Vitez. I received information that a meeting had been held in the International Hotel in Zenica. And that it was being held. And when I arrived at that meeting, I received information that Zivko Totic had been kidnapped on that day. It was then that I received this information for the first time, that Zivko Totic had been kidnapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you were on your way from a meeting in Vitez, and while you were en route you received this information?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the way back from Vitez, I received information that a meeting was being held at the International. And it was at that meeting at the International that I learned about the kidnapping of Mr. Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you receive this information while you were en route via a radio or a cell phone? How did you know to go to the International Hotel?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The European monitors told me that this meeting was being held in the International Hotel. I did not have a radio set, and I could not communicate with anybody. The European monitors had a radio set in the vehicle that I was driving in. I could not communicate with anybody. I did not have a radio set on me to be able to communicate with anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. So you were in a European Union Monitoring Mission vehicle coming back from Vitez, and you were informed by the European monitors about the situation, and they took you to the International Hotel?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said there was a meeting at the Hotel International, but they didn't tell me what the meeting was discussing. They didn't tell me that Zivko Totic had been kidnapped. I found that out from people who attended the meeting at the International Hotel, not from ECMM monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, what do you recall being told about the kidnapping of Zivko Totic at the International Hotel on 15 April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information was given me that Mr. Zivko Totic had been kidnapped in the early morning hours of the 15th of April 1993, and that extensive measures were being taken to find his whereabouts, to detect the perpetrators. But at that point, it was still unknown who the kidnappers were or where he was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So on the 15th of April 1993, you had no specific information about who took him or where they took him?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I personally had no such knowledge, and from what I could hear at the meeting, even the people at the meeting didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time shortly thereafter where you had certain suspicions concerning this kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was absolutely astounded that this kidnapping could have happened in Zenica because Zenica was pretty quiet and safe. The representatives of HVO could move around freely, and there had been no problems before. The Croats and the Muslims and even the Serbs in Zenica coexisted peacefully, as far as that is possible with a war going on. But there had been no particular problems in Zenica. And I was amazed that this could have happened in a town with properly-functioning civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, where at that time in April 1993, where was Colonel Totic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the precise location. I don't know where the command post -- where his command post was. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It was in Zenica, though. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Whether it was in the centre of the town itself or in the periphery, I don't know. But yes, it was in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the 3rd Corps headquarters were also in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you don't know where this HVO brigade headquarters were located even though it was in the same town as your corps headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I had no particular problems with the HVO of Zenica, and I didn't attach much importance to Zenica as such. Everything was quiet and normal. I didn't think it necessary to even inspect the command of that brigade, the conditions of accommodation. I didn't believe that was necessary, and I, therefore, did not visit the headquarters of the HVO or remember their location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, what steps, if any, did you take after the 15th of April 1993 to determine who was responsible for the kidnapping of Colonel Totic or where Colonel Totic was located?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information that the civilian police were searching for him very intensively because the incident happened in the area where civilian authorities were responsible, and that the civilian police was in charge, assisted perhaps by the military police. To what extent they were assisted by military police, I don't know. It goes into their expertise. I already testified before this Court that the civilian police often cooperated with the military police on specific assignments, and I believe the necessary degree of cooperation between the civilian and military police had been attained. However, the primary responsibility lay with the civilian police because life in that area was normal; people normally went to work, children went to school, civilian authorities functioned properly, normally in the conditions of war. And the incident was not within the competence of the military police. It was quite logical that the civilian police should be searching for the kidnapped person. As far as I know, the investigation and search for Zivko Totic was handled by the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, you told us the incident was not within the competence of the military police; it was quite logical that the civilian police should be searching for the kidnapped person. And my next question is: Why was it logical for the civilian police to be searching and why was this incident not within the competence of the military police?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have already explained. The civilian authorities were in operation. There were no combat operations in the area. Therefore, it was quite logical, and I believe the main activity was handled by the civilian police. But I also said that the civilian police cooperated with the military police. As to the volume of that cooperation in the case of Zivko Totic, this concerns operative activities that I had no access to at the time. It was not my job to go into operative details of investigation in the case of Zivko Totic. That's why I said it was logical for the civilian police to handle it. Zivko Totic was not a member of the BH Army. And as I said here, the 3rd Corps was responsible only for its own troops. Zivko Totic was a member of a different army. If he had been a member of the BH Army, certainly our forces would have worked on the case. But since that was not the case, it was not logical for the military police to be the primary mover of this investigation. The primary vehicle of the investigation was the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you personally take any steps to determine the whereabouts of Zivko Totic or who was responsible for kidnapping him? You personally?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, I had an entirely different mission. Even at that time, I had an entirely different mission. I was a member of the joint commission, and my main job involved the meetings of the joint commission. This was followed by a very difficult situation because the next day, the HVO attacked the Ahmici village. So in the tactical and operative sense, this consumed my attention. I did not focus on the investigation in the case of Zivko Totic. I did not personally get involved in this investigation. I didn't do anything personally to investigate. I only would have welcomed any information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you have any discussions with Colonel Robert Stewart of BritBat concerning the kidnapping of Zivko Totic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I talked to many people. Whenever somebody raised the issue of the kidnapping of Zivko Totic, I never skirted around it, and I didn't try to avoid. But if Mr. Bob Stewart, whom I hold in very high esteem, told you that I discussed the kidnapping of Zivko Totic with him, I have no reason not to believe him. But it's not like it was the only subject of our discussions. We discussed the general situation in our very frequent contacts. We were in touch all the time, especially because his officers provided me with transportation, as a member of the joint commission, and I had opportunity to meet him very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I take it, then, sir, from your answer that you wouldn't rule out the possibility that you spoke to Colonel Bob Stewart about the Zivko Totic kidnapping? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, I don't rule out the possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did there come a time when you took any steps to deliver any messages or information from the foreigners concerning the kidnapping of Zivko Totic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not mediate in the passing of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know a person named Zvonko Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Mr. Zvonko Vukovic because he was a member of the joint command that was set up by the HVO and the ABiH in which both sides were represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you deliver a letter to Mr. Vukovic in the PTT building in Travnik and inform him that it was from the mujahedin and that you were only the mailman?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that detail, and I don't believe it happened because I said already I did not mediate in negotiations between the kidnappers and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you turn to Document P417 in the documents that we provided to you this morning, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps while the witness is doing that, Mr. President, if the usher could return the 3rd Corps original log, which is still in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you have P417 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found the document. I have read the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm seeing it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you look towards the bottom of the document where it says, "P. S.," it seems to indicate, sir, that you personally delivered this letter to Mr. Zvonko Vukovic in the joint operations centre.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true. I did not hand over any documents to Mr. Zvonko Vukovic, and I see this, that this was typed on two different typewriters. The postscript was added to the text, typed on a different typewriter. And I'm seeing this document for the first time, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
