utterances.text: Sir, could you look at the top of P417 where there appears to be a header that a facsimile machine would put on a document. The number beginning with 3-8 -- the number actually is 3872712903. Do you know where that fax number operated in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't know this fax number from which this was sent. I don't know this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, 387 is the country code for Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 387 is the country code for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you know where the location or city code, what the city code is for Zenica?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's 72. 71 is the code for Sarajevo. 72, I believe, is the code for Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you don't recall delivering any document to Mr. Zvonko Vukovic in late April 1993. Is that your testimony here today, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is my testimony before this Court, that I did not give this document to Mr. Zvonko Vukovic, or any document of similar content.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, did there ever come a time when you were at a meeting in Uskoplje with BritBat and Mr. Totic was in attendance? And I'm talking about after he was released.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember meetings that were held after the Washington Agreement was signed, in Gornji Vakuf, in the -- on the base of the BritBat. As far as I remember, those were meetings of the joint committee of which I was a member for a while representing the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And the head of our delegation on that joint commission was General Fikret Muslimovic, if I'm not mistaken. I remember there were also representatives of the HVO. I can't remember who their team leader was, whether it was General Roso or somebody else. I can't remember. But I do recall that I attended a number of these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me, sir, try the question again. I'm referring to a meeting in Uskoplje that was attended by Mr. Zivko Totic, and I believe BritBat hosted this meeting. Do you recall any meetings in Uskoplje that Mr. Zivko Totic attended?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the meetings of the joint committee, then I do remember. If you mean some other kind of meeting, I don't remember. But I remember that the meetings of the joint committee that was set up after the Washington Agreement were attended also by Mr. Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with Mr. Zivko Totic at any of those meetings about the kidnapping of Mr. Totic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember any discussions involving the kidnapping of Mr. Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I'd like to turn now to the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and its formation, and you've testified about this and you've actually been shown a document, which is again before you if you need to consult it. It's P124. This is the document where you propose the formation of the 7th Muslim Brigade in November 1992. Do you remember testifying about that and seeing that document? Again, it's P124. It should be the first document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first document is P133, not 124. I am leafing through, and I still can't find 124.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps it's the very front document.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not marked. That's what confused me. Yes, but it is the first document. I just found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, this is the document dated 18 November 1992 in which you proposed forming the 7th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you also made some recommendations about persons to be appointed brigade commander and chief of staff. And you see that down in the fourth or fifth paragraph of this document. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. It's under numbers 1 and 2 in this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There's actually two numbers 1 and two numbers 2. Can you tell us who you recommended to be the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise this document. I suggested here Mr. Mahmut Karalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for the post of chief of staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade, you proposed Asim Koricic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, who was Mahmut Karalic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mahmut Karalic was an inhabitant of Zenica. I knew that he was good at organising, that he was able to organise and lead a unit. That was my understanding and my idea behind this proposal to the superior command to appoint this gentleman Mahmut Karalic commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, who, in fact, became the first commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the first commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade was Mr. Koricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The transcript said, sir, that you said it was Mr. Koricic. Is that correct, or was it Mr. Karalic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Koricic, Koricic. I suggested Karalic to become commander. However, when the order came from the superior command, the appointment was given to Koricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, prior to Asim Koricic being appointed commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, did you know him? And if so, how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had superficial information about -- I had almost no information about Mr. Asim Koricic. I knew that he was from Krajina, that he had certain knowledge that would enable him to join the 7th Muslim Brigade. That was my information. That's why I suggested that he should be appointed chief of staff of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us that you had -- that you had --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, sir, that you had certain knowledge that would enable him to join the 7th. What information or knowledge was that that you had?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, he had already participated in combat in various areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't know where exactly. I did not have precise information. I also knew that he was an experienced fighter. This was the information that I had. That's why I suggested that he should be the chief of staff of this brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, where had he gained this experience as a fighter? Or where had he participated in combat?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have precise information. I didn't know where exactly he participated in combat. I had information, however, that he participated in the defence of Karaula. I don't know how he had found himself there after the fall of Jajce when the aggressor took the town of Jajce. I've already spoken about these difficult moments. I had information that he had been defending the territory threatened by the aggressor in the general area of Vlasic. I knew that he was a seasoned soldier who was at that moment not a member of the Territorial Defence staff. I've already said that in Karaula and in the Vlasic plateau, everybody was engaged. The refugees from Krajina and Jajce were engaged. Everybody defended the territory there. Central Bosnia was being defended in the area of the Vlasic plateau and Karaula. And this is the information that I had, that he had participated in combat in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, Asim Koricic had been with the MOS prior to this appointment to the 7th Muslim Brigade. Do you agree or disagree with that statement? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't rule that out. I've already said that MOS was never part of the Territorial Defence. This is something that I have already testified about. I've said that people organised themselves on a voluntary basis to defend Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't know that he was a MOS commander, but I wouldn't rule it out. I only know that if the MOS had existed, it was not part of the Territorial Defence. I didn't know that he was a MOS commander. I didn't know that the MOS ever existed in that area. I never personally saw him. I only knew that everybody joined the defence of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if at the point Asim Koricic was appointed commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, if any soldiers that he had previously fought with followed him and joined that brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information. I can't remember how Asim Koricic was appointed the commander of this brigade. It was up to the superior command to decide that. Maybe they had more accurate information. Maybe they were aware of him having appropriate military education. I, myself, did not have that information at that point in time. I can't answer your question because I don't have this information. I'm not aware of the thing that you've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, at the time the 7th Muslim Brigade was formed and the other units of the 3rd Corps were formed, the post of chief of staff at the brigade level was an important one because there weren't deputy commanders at the brigade level. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And so, in effect, the chief of staff would be the person who would assume command if something happened to the brigade commander or the brigade commander was temporarily not with the unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, to the best of your recollection, who was the chief of staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade upon its formation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, when the orders from the superior command arrived, the person who was appointed the chief of staff was Mr. Amir Kubura, if my memory serves me well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, what, if anything, did you know about Mr. Amir Kubura at the time he was appointed chief of staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any special information at that time. The only information that I had was that he was born in Kakanj, that he was an officer of the former JNA, that he had completed military education, and that he had joined the defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is all I knew at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, do you recall the approximate dates that Mr. Koricic and Mr. Kubura were appointed commander and chief of staff respectively of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall the month and year?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was in January, or maybe even in late December. I can't remember exactly whether it was in late December 1992 or January 1993. I would sooner say that it was in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, there came a point, did there not, that Asim Koricic left Bosnia in the spring of 1993 and did not return for the duration of the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I don't know when he left or when he returned. I only remember that for a while he was not in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that he left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, I don't recall the dates when he left or when he returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, I suggest to you that Mr. Asim Koricic left Central Bosnia on the 31st of March 1993, and that he went to Croatia and was involved in importing foreigners into Central Bosnia, and that he did so on behalf of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But certainly in the absence of Mr. Koricic, Amir Kubura would be in command of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Do you have any doubts about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the appointment of the brigade commander, it would be the chief of staff who would stand in for the brigade commander. This was part of his job description. This was part of his mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, at some point after Mr. Asim Koricic left Bosnia, Mr. Kubura was, in fact, appointed commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you have a recollection approximately when that happened?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you a couple of questions concerning your testimony in the Kordic trial. You recall testifying in January 2000 in the Kordic trial?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, you were asked some questions in that case. You were cross-examined by Mr. Naumovski on the 25th of January 2000, and he asked you some questions about the 7th Muslim Brigade. Do you remember him asking you those questions about the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember him asking you questions about Asim Koricic as the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember saying under oath in the Kordic and Cerkez trial that Mr. Asim Koricic was never the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't rule out the possibility that I said that. If I had, it must have been a huge slip of the tongue on my part. I sometimes do it here, depending on the questions put to me, especially if people insist on me saying something, I tend to make slips of the tongue. I don't rule out the possibility that I made a slip of the tongue at that time. There may have been such answers. If I had said that, I apologise to the Trial Chamber. If I had been aware of my slip of the tongue at the time, I would have corrected myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, actually, on page 12.910 of the Kordic transcript of the 25th of January 2000, you stated that Mr. Koricic was not the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade on two separate occasions on that page of the transcript. And I would like to read this part of the transcript to you and see if, in fact, what you said in the Kordic trial was a slip of the tongue. Again, for the record, this is page 12.910, case number IT-95-14/2-T, 25 January 2000, cross-examination by Mr. Naumovski, line 1. Question: "I'm referring to the time when Asim Koricic commanded the 7th Muslim Brigade, so that would be -- the brigade was founded on the 1st of December 1992, so that would be that period until sometime in the summer 1993." Answer: "I believe you made a mistake because Asim Koricic was never a commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And the El Mujahid was founded, as far as I know, in late 1993 or perhaps early 1994, and when it was established, it was placed under the command of the 3rd Corps." Question: "If I understood you well, you say that Asim Koricic was never the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade." Answer: "No, Asim Koricic was never the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade." Those are lines 1 through 16 of page 12.910 in the Kordic and Cerkez trial. Now, sir, was that exchange simply a slip of the tongue or a misunderstanding of the questions that were put to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I claim that it was a slip of the tongue. Now, I can see what I said at the time. I did not have a possibility to follow the transcript because the transcript is in English. Whatever I say is in English on the transcript. I am not in a position to follow the transcript of my words, but this was certainly a slip of the tongue. It was a slip of the tongue on my part. I apologise, Your Honours. It is possible for me to make such slips of the tongue. For example, I was mistaken on several occasions here. I remember very well when you asked me about 1992 or 1993, and I thought you were referring to the years 2002 and 2003. Slips of the tongue are possible, and I kindly ask the Trial Chamber to take this into account. So yes, this was a slip of the tongue on my part. You have to understand that questions put to me are very difficult, very complex, often repetitive, and I am being asked here to remember things that happened 10 or 11 years ago. You're asking me about the exact times of the day, the exact times of the night, the dates, the names of the people, their description. And this is a huge frustration. It makes me frustrated, and this frustration repeats every year or every two years or so. And it is possible for me to be prone to making slips of the tongue in such situations. I don't exclude that possibility. However, whenever I'm aware of having made a slip of the tongue, whenever I am reminded of the events by way of documents being presented to me, then I apologise. I admit that I have made a mistake. In this case, this slip of the tongue is so huge that I really can't understand how I could allow myself at that moment to make such a slip of the tongue, especially now that I see the documents and the reports that I saw last week. I can really say, and I confirm, that this was a slip of the tongue on my part, and I sincerely apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, let me just ask you one follow-up question with respect to your answer. In the Kordic trial, sir, were you hearing the interpretation in your language or were you trying to follow the questions that were put to you by reading the English transcript in light of the fact that you've told us several times you don't read English? Were you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. answering the questions in response to what you heard via the interpretation or were you trying to answer the questions based on reading the rolling transcript in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always try to answer questions put to me in my own language because I can't speak or read English. I'm not looking at the screen because I can't read what it says on the screen. That's why I'm always focussed on what I receive in my own language. I do not refer to the transcript. I don't refer to the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to your recollection, were you referring to the screen in Kordic, the English transcript on the screen, or were you responding to the questions by way of the oral interpretation that you heard in the headphones? Again, in the Kordic case, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was answering in my own language, and I was not trying to follow the transcript on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At any rate, sir, your testimony, and I believe your position now is quite clear, Asim Koricic was, in fact, the first commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And he held that post from sometime in late 1992 or early 1993 until he departed Bosnia, whenever that was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did hold that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the first chief of staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade was Amir Kubura, and he held that post from, again, sometime in late December 1992 or early January 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already testified that I can't remember the exact dates. That's why I wouldn't want to say something that I'm not a hundred per cent sure of. I don't remember those dates when Mr. Amir Kubura was appointed the chief of staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But Mr. Kubura would be the acting commander in the absence of Mr. Koricic during 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the moment when a new commander is appointed, in the absence of Mr. Asim Koricic, it was Mr. Amir Kubura who performed those duties. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in this instance of the 7th Muslim Brigade in 1993, when we talk about the moment a new commander is appointed, in fact, for the 7th Muslim Brigade in 1993, the new commander was the former chief of staff, Mr. Amir Kubura. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep on insisting that I should repeat what I have already stated. I am really tired. This has been a long day. My feeling is that you want me to make another slip of the tongue that you would base your future questions on. I can't remember the date when Amir Kubura was appointed the chief of staff of the brigade. You have to understand the situation in which all this happened. I've already spoken at great length about all that. I can't remember the dates and you have to accept that. I'm just telling you what I remember and what I know. What I can't remember and what I don't know, I can't share with you, and I can't claim any of that before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't ask you in this question about the date; I simply asked you if it was your recollection that Mr. Kubura was appointed the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade in 1993 following the departure of Mr. Koricic, whenever that was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I am not sure of any of the dates, Mr. Amir Kubura was appointed commander after Mr. Asim Koricic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. This might be the appropriate spot for our next technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is almost half past 12.00. The witness will have a half an hour to rest. We will resume at 1.00 exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall now resume. Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, I have a few more questions about the 7th Muslim Brigade. And I would ask you, sir, if you recall what has been described as an assassination attempt against Amir Kubura in July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would object to this question. It doesn't arise from the examination-in-chief, and I don't see the legal foundation that the Prosecution has laid in order to put such a question and contrast this with what the witness has been saying so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you want to put a question to the witness about the assassination of General Kubura. The Defence objects to that question, and they say you can't put that question because it doesn't arise from the examination-in-chief. This issue was never raised either directly or indirectly during the examination-in-chief. What is your response to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, it relates to the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, and what I am intending on doing is showing the witness Prosecution Exhibit P233, which is a milinfosum that discusses this and also discusses some other issues relating to the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution says that Exhibit P233, which is a milinfosum, is relative on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecution wishes to show the witness a document. However, I would like to point out again that we did not put a single question to the witness with regard to this document or to this issue, and I don't see the legal foundation for the Prosecutor's line of questioning or showing the document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges have deliberated, and they say that it is in the interests of justice to ask the question. The document is allowed, and the Defence themselves have mentioned this assassination attempt. There is a document from the foreign source that talk about that, and the witness is indeed mentioned in this document. So Mr. Mundis, you have the floor. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, do you remember this incident in July 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have information as to what transpired. I know there was an incident. I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. I'm simply asking if you recall being made aware of the incident. I ask this question, sir, if you could turn, please, to P233, and towards the end of that document you will see a heading indicating "7th Muslim Brigade." It's paragraph 11 of P233, and I would ask you, please, sir, if you could take a look at that paragraph and read paragraph 11 of Prosecution Exhibit P233. And I have a couple of questions for you about the contents of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I was aware of the report about this incident. I said I had some information. If I said that I learned about the incident, then it would mean that I'm aware of the details. So I'm going to read the paragraph that you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's, then, if you would prefer to do it this way, I can simply ask you some questions. Did you play down this incident as merely being an altercation in discussions that you had with any liaison officers of UNPROFOR or BritBat?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not aware of the incident. I had information that this was an incident which in my mind was not a major problem because I didn't have information as to what actually transpired. I don't know what occurred on that day in the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember telling a liaison officer of BritBat or UNPROFOR that this was simply an altercation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how the British officer portrayed this in his report. I will allow for his free interpretation of our conversation. He can say that this was his opinion based on the conversation that we had. I can't even remember that I ever spoke to any of these officers about this issue. I do not rule out that possibility because I had a lot of conversations with officers coming from various countries, including British officers who were part of the UN mission. I don't exclude the possibility that I spoke to him; however, I can't recall that this issue was raised. I can't recall what I told this officer about that. I can't remember this issue being raised in a conversation with an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this: Do you recall at any point in time in July of 1993 any orders being given by the 3rd Corps that commanders should not talk on the subject of the 7th Muslim Brigade? And I'm talking about to speak to international representatives about the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we did not issue such an order. If there was such an order, I wasn't aware of it. I don't know that we issued an order forbidding anybody to talk about the 7th Muslim Brigade or with the 7th Muslim Brigade. We did not forbid anybody to talk about any of the units. I believed then and I still believe that there were no secrets that should not have been discussed. I don't remember any such order ever being issued by the 3rd Corps, forbidding people to talk with or about the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to draw your attention to June 23rd, 1993. There was a meeting of a number of officers of the 3rd Corps and its subordinate units held in Biljesevo on that day. And the minutes of that meeting reflect the fact that you were there.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I can't remember the date, June 23rd, 1993. I don't know what happened on that day. It is possible that there was a meeting. I don't exclude that possibility. If you have the minutes of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that meeting, then obviously there's no reason for me to doubt that a meeting was held in Biljesevo on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you please turn to Exhibit P429. Now, sir, can you look at the first page of this document. Do you see at the top of this document where it indicates -- in the original, where it indicates the persons who were present?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see that on the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, you see the name of your commander, Enver Hadzihasanovic; the chief of staff, Mr. Mekic; yourself; General Alagic; Mr. Dugalic; Mr. Kubura; among others being present at this meeting. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. I've just read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, the upper right portion, it indicates that this was at Biljesevo on 23 June 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the heading indicates that it's a meeting of officers of the 3rd Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, in the Bosnian-language version of this document, if you could turn, please, to the page with the stamped number ending - it's at the top - 4203. The full number is 01814203. Are you on that page, sir?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, about halfway down, it indicates 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade with the initials "Chief of Staff Kubura." Do you see that part of this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you please, to yourself, read that section under 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, and it continues to the next page, and I would ask you, please, to read up until it says "Kelestura" which is almost at the bottom of the next page. If you could just review those minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read the part from the indication "7th Muslim Brigade" to the part where it says "Kelestura."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you see under the part that says "proposal," there's reference to "hiring foreign nationals." I ask you, sir, if you remember that being discussed at this meeting, and I ask in addition, if you do remember this being discussed, if you can fill us in on any additional details that you remember being discussed about hiring foreign nationals as of the 23rd of June 1993 in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, at this meeting on this day, 23rd May [as interpreted] 1993, the issue of foreigners was again raised in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. As far as I remember, we were provided with somewhat more detailed information about the problem. We were told that this problem was getting bigger by the day, and that it represented a problem for the 3rd Corps. I remember that on the 13th of June, that is, before this meeting, the corps command sent a letter to the supreme command staff, asking them to take urgent measures because the corps command did not have the means to oppose the foreigners who were turning into a big problem. I've already testified to that fact. Around the 16th of June 1993, the supreme command staff provided us with information according to which these foreigners should be placed under control. And if they refused to do so, that they should be sent to the area of Igman. I've already spoken about that in great length. At this meeting, if I'm not mistaken, this issue was indeed raised. And after this order, at the level of the corps command, we evaluated the situation. I have testified to that as well. I've told you what this would have meant for the 3rd Corps. According to our estimate, these foreigners had a lot of influence with the people. I've already told you why. They distributed food amongst our population. They distributed money. They married our girls. And we believed at the time that a lot of Bosniaks rallied around those foreigners. We did not know what their number was. And we thought at the time that this would mean the opening of the third front. This is what we discussed, and I believe that the issue of foreigners was presented within that context. And the engagement of foreigners within the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps was mentioned within that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, before it disappears off the screen, line 24 on page 62 makes reference to this meeting being the 23rd of May. I believe that the document clearly indicates it was the 23rd of June 1993. I simply want to clear that up. This meeting was on the 23rd of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this meeting in Biljesevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 23rd of June. If I said May, that was a slip of the tongue, or maybe it was misinterpreted. It says here that this was in June 1993, and this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, what was being discussed was a follow-on to the order received on the 16th of June 1993 from the supreme command staff. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a meeting after the 16th of June. In other words, this meeting followed the events on the 16th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you look at the line right after the one that says "hiring foreign nationals," there's a question put into these minutes. And it says, "Will we continue to hire them because they receive ammunition?" What was that all about?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the commander was saying. My interpretation would be that they were still active in the area of the 3rd Corps, that they were armed, that they had weapons. This was a problem which was probably a problem not only for the commander of the 7th, but for all of us. It was our joint problem. It says here that they received ammunition. I don't know what the brigade commander was referring to when he said that. I know that ammunition was being purchased on the black market and that people obtained arms, ammunition, and other things on the black market. You know that in the times of war, the black market flourishes. You can buy anything, even a plane on the black market. We in the 3rd Corps were not in the position to obtain enough ammunition or weapons, and the black market was very active. People cooperated with the aggressor, there were individuals who cooperated with the HVO, they purchased arms and weapons from them as well. We did not have any control over these individuals who were war profiteers. I believe that the reference was made to these people, and that's how the foreigners also obtained ammunition. I claim with full responsibility that the 3rd Corps of the BiH Army did not distribute ammunition to these foreigners. If the foreigners had ammunition, this ammunition did not come from the 3rd Corps. I am absolutely certain of that, and I claim that with full responsibility before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, sir, again, looking at this sentence of these minutes, it says, and I'd like you to focus on this part, "Will we continue to hire them?" That language, sir, suggests that there were foreigners in the 7th Muslim Brigade prior to the 23rd of June 1993, does it not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. I claim that foreigners --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I wanted to object a while ago because the way he paraphrases Mr. Kubura's words, it doesn't mention the engagement of these foreigners within the 7th Brigade. This issue was raised in a general context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence for General Kubura has objected. They say that the words of General Kubura do not say what the Prosecution says they do. We have a problem here. When we put a question to the witness, do we expect the witness to say who said that and whether all the officers who were present at the meeting, do they all ask the question whether we should continue to recruit and engage the foreigners? Who was it who asked that question? Was it General Kubura, the commander of the 3rd Corps? The whole body of officers? General Merdan, you see the question that was raised. In your view, who was it who asked that question? Who raised this issue? The person who mentions this, was that the person who just summarises what had been said up to then, or was this just a single question put by somebody, General Kubura, and somebody else? As far as you can remember, what can you tell us? There's this question, but there is also the next question, which is very important. What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have to read everything in order to be able to provide you with a precise answer. I just -- I've just told you what I read. I based my answer on the part I was instructed to read. My comments are based on that, and this is how I attempted to answer the Prosecutor's question. I've tried to see this problem within the context of the overall problem with foreigners in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. If this is what has been recorded as General Kubura's words, I see that he mentions the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. So this is the problem of the 3rd Corps. I've already testified to that effect. The 7th Muslim Brigade did not have an area of responsibility. It was a manoeuvre unit. So this is a problem for the entire 3rd Corps, not for the 7th Muslim Brigade as such. I've already spoken about that at great length. I don't know whether this is a summary of all the discussions dealing with foreigners. It's very difficult for me to answer this question. I don't remember that the overall conclusion of this meeting was the problem of foreigners. This problem was mentioned as a problem -- one of the problems for the 3rd Corps, but there were many other problems. This is just one of the problems that we were aware of and we were trying to find a solution to this problem. I've already Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. spoken about that. I've also mentioned the ways that the 3rd Corps proposed to deal with this issue. The foreigners were not the only issue on the agenda. It was just one of the issues. This is my opinion about a document that I've had the opportunity to look at only briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, let's try to look at this in a slightly different way. When the 3rd Corps had meetings of the various subordinate units, such as this one on the 23rd of June 1993, I suggest to you that the way these minutes are structured indicates that what happened was the corps commander made some initial comments, and then, in effect, they went around the room and the different unit commanders spoke. And I say that because simply looking at the document seems to indicate that that was the way the meetings were conducted. And my question is, as a general rule, would that be the way these meetings were conducted?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in principle. There were also meetings around one topical issue. For example, under 1 here, the issue is the situation in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. So this was one of the topics of this meeting. A number of problems were mentioned at this meeting as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, if you turn back, sir, to the early part of this document, it seems to indicate, after it lists who all is in attendance, the 3rd Corps commander, General Hadzihasanovic, spoke and spoke about goals and questions for the meeting and the order, and it says under Order, "five minutes for each commander to present the situation." And then we have a number of commands with the names of the commanders of those units, and it appears as though it systematically follows that each command was represented by a senior officer of that command and presented the situation for that subordinate unit.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one may conclude that. From what you have just said, one may arrive at such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's go back, then, sir, to the portion under the heading "proposal" under the subheading or heading "7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, chief of staff Kubura." I would like to ask you, sir, if the fact that it says "We will continue to hire them" [sic] with respect to foreigners, reflects the fact that foreigners were part of the 3rd Corps prior to the 23rd of June 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will share my opinion with you and my knowledge with regard to this issue that you have raised here. I can read here the following: Will they be sent to Igman? Will they continue being engaged in the area of the 3rd Corps? So there's no reference to the area of responsibility of the 7th Brigade but of the 3rd Corps, which means that we do have information that they are engaged and that they are a problem. But they're not engaged in the units of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It says in the document, "Will we continue to hire them?" And I'm asking you about that language "continue," that word "continue," whether it was the 3rd Corps or the 7th or any other subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we have an interpretation problem, but the words are very important here. The Defence team for General Kubura want to object. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have just -- I just wanted to point to this problem. I believe that we have an interpretation or translation problem because in the B/C/S, we have a question. "Are we going to continue engaging them?" In the English translation, it says, "We will continue to hire them." So it's not a question in the English version. So maybe the witness could elaborate on this linguistic issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I must respond to that. The English translation says, "Will we continue to hire them because they receive ammunition?" The English translation clearly indicates it's a question. My question to the witness is focussing on the word "continue," "Will we continue to hire them because they receive ammunition?" I believe it's a very straightforward question. "Will we continue to hire them?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, could you please read in your language, in your own language, the sentence in your language, and we will receive the interpretation of what you read in your language. Can you read the two sentences. In English, there are two questions: One which is relative to the ammunition, and the second one is a double question in which the question is asked whether they will be sent to the Mount Igman or will they continue combat operations in the area of operations of the 3rd Corps. Can you please read in your own language these two questions, and we will receive the interpretation, the official interpretation, of what you read. General, can you please read these two sentences.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Will they continue being engaged because they receive ammunition?" "Will they go to Igman, or will they continue carrying out combat operations in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps?" This is what I read as questions. These are questions. Questions are being raised whether they will be engaged, whether they will continue being, whether they will remain in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. It doesn't say here that they are on the strength of the BiH Army unit or the 3rd Corps of the BiH Army. They are beyond control, and they act beyond control. I've spoken at great length about that. This is a question. Are they going to still be engaged? My interpretation is if they're engaged in any way, because we don't know who is it who engages them and how, I've already spoken about that at great length. Our mission was not to allow for them to be engaged beyond the control of the 3rd Corps. As far as I know, they were not under the control of either the 3rd Corps or the 7th Brigade. I don't know who armed these foreigners, who provided them with ammunition. Somebody must have provided them with ammunition. They probably purchased ammunition on the black market. They had arms. They were engaged in combat operations on their own. But this was not under our control. I've already explained to this Trial Chamber what the command of the 3rd Corps did in order to place them under their control. This was such a huge problem that the 3rd Corps command could not resolve it on their own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have explained. The only difference that I see in the English translation and the translation in the transcript, instead of saying "in the zone of operations," you say "in the area of responsibility." That's the only difference that I see. Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the main difference between the written translation and the interpretation on the screen and the text in our language is the fact that -- is in who is going to engage whom? In our B/C/S version, the subject is impersonal. There's no subject. The question is whether they will still continue being engaged. It doesn't say -- are we still continuing engaging them? The first-person plural in the English version does not exist in the original. The subject is impersonal. It is nonexistent. This is possible in B/C/S. In all the three questions, there is no subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence explains to us that the "we" which could have been construed as the we, military, the 3rd Corps, does not exist in the B/C/S, that it is impersonal in the original. This is the impression that we got. The "we" in English is not the "we," the military. It should be considered as a nonexistent subject, as an impersonal question. It doesn't imply that this question was asked by somebody from the 3rd Corps. Mr. Mundis, we have already gone beyond our allocated time. Maybe we can continue tomorrow morning. Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. President, because this is -- this type of issue has arisen in other trials, I am aware in other cases where both the transcript and the document itself can be presented to the head of CLSS who is the Tribunal's, if you will, linguistic expert for an absolutely authoritative determination, both as to the document as well as the testimony of the past, say, 10 or 15 minutes. CLSS has, in previous cases, provided such linguistic expertise because of the importance of this subject. And I believe that that might be very helpful to all the parties concerned so that we can an authoritative explanation or translation of this document as well as what's been said here in the past few minutes. Because I believe the Chamber is aware, this is a potentially very important issue. And with all due respect to my colleagues, we do have experts in the Bosnian-English and French languages who are available to assist us with this very matter. I believe perhaps the Registrar can assist us with getting that to the appropriate senior-level person in CLSS who can assist us with this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges will discuss the matter briefly. --- Break taken at 1.48 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has discussed the issue of translation. We believe that the Registrar should ask the CLSS to verify this before tomorrow's session, which starts at 9.00. We will have the official translation of the sentences contained in the handwritten document on pages 429 in B/C/S, and that these questions should be translated into English and, if possible, into French. This will provide us with double verification. So that these questions should be translated from B/C/S into English, and B/C/S into French. If it cannot be done from B/C/S into French, it should be done from English into French, and that this should be done by the person most responsible within the CLSS [as interpreted]. They have a whole afternoon at their disposal to do that, so I suppose this should not be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Registrar indicates that there is a mistake in the transcript. The number of the page is wrong. The text that should be translated is the text on pages 4 and 5 in English; and in B/C/S, this text can be found on 01814204. And the number of the Exhibit is P431. Tomorrow, we shall have the official translation. We shall resume tomorrow at -- The number of the document is P429. We are all tired, I believe. So a verbal decision should be taken. But before that, could I ask the usher to bring the general out of the courtroom. General, we shall see you at tomorrow's session which starts at 9.00. The usher is going to take you out of the courtroom. General, tomorrow, Wednesday, I would like to tell you, tomorrow, the session starts at 9.00 in the morning, and at 12.30 we will make a break, a lunch break. We will continue at 2.00, and we shall work until 7.00 in the afternoon. Take a good rest because tomorrow we will be working long hours, from 9 to 12.30, and then from 2.00 to 7.00 in the afternoon. You may leave the courtroom now. I'm going to ask the usher -- I'm going to ask the Registrar to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is an issue that is still pending. Will the Prosecution ask for the admission of the map that was marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, we will, Mr. President. And we would also ask for the admission of the larger map that was marked yesterday. We would ask for the admission of both of those maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want to do it now? Do you want to wait until the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We can wait, that's fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall wait, then. It is 2.00. I thank everybody, and I invite you to come back tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of December, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.
